Recommended Highlights This Week

1. Singapore River Festival 2026 begins – 11 September, Boat Quay/Clarke Quay/Robertson Quay

2. AL!VE Artisans Market – 12–13 September, National Stadium

3. Tian Tian Chicken Rice – new outlet at Jewel Changi Airport

4. SKAI's Toy Story Afternoon Tea – through 30 November

5. Singapore Gallery Month & SLA25 Trail – both close 13 September

Events & Festivals

Overall Summary

The river takes centre stage this week as the Singapore River Festival 2026 begins on the 11th – its 10th edition, dubbed The Quay Collective, spreading across Boat Quay, Clarke Quay and Robertson Quay with each precinct taking on its own distinct character. The weekend also brings AL!VE Artisans Market back to the National Stadium, and families have a genuinely good reason to detour through Jewel Changi Airport now that Tian Tian Chicken Rice – the Maxwell Food Centre institution once praised by Anthony Bourdain – has opened there. This is also the closing week for two of our longer-running recommendations: Singapore Gallery Month and the SLA25 Rediscovery Trail both wrap up on the 13th, so this is the last chance to point guests toward either before they're gone.

Singapore River Festival 2026 – The Quay Collective

Now in its 10th edition, the Singapore River Festival celebrates the people, places and stories that have shaped the Singapore River. This year's theme, The Quay Collective, spreads the festival across three distinct zones, each with its own character: the Entertainment Zone at Boat Quay, the Expression Zone at Clarke Quay, and the Lifestyle & Wellness Zone at Robertson Quay. Rather than one central stage, the festival breathes extra life into the riverside over ten days through immersive experiences, performances and activities unique to each stretch of the river.

Event Date: 11–20 September 2026

Location: Boat Quay, Clarke Quay & Robertson Quay

Admission: Free

Best For: Couples / Families / Free Activities / Riverside Guests

Concierge Recommendation: A strong recommendation for any guest staying near the river – suggest picking one zone per evening rather than trying to cover all three at once, since each has a genuinely different atmosphere.

AL!VE Artisans Market

A recurring weekend market bringing together local artisans, makers and small brands at the National Stadium – a relaxed, browse-at-your-own-pace alternative to the bigger festival crowds happening elsewhere in the city this month.

Event Date: 12–13 September 2026

Time: 11:00am–7:00pm

Location: 1 Stadium Place, National Stadium, The Kallang, Singapore 397628

Admission: Free

Best For: Shoppers / Couples / Something Low-Key

Concierge Recommendation: A good lower-key alternative for guests who want browsing and shopping rather than a full festival atmosphere – easy to combine with a Kallang waterfront walk.

Singapore Botanic Gardens & Fort Canning Park Heritage Festival

Marking 11 years since the Singapore Botanic Gardens' UNESCO World Heritage listing, this nine-day festival spans both the Gardens and Fort Canning Park with music, art, guided tours and workshops. The headline addition this year is EnlighTEN, the Gardens' first-ever light show, transforming five iconic spaces after dark. A free self-guided Heritage Rally (stamp-collecting across both parks) runs throughout, and a free shuttle bus connects the two sites on weekends.

Event Date: 5–13 September 2026 (daily, 9:00am–10:00pm)

Location: Singapore Botanic Gardens & Fort Canning Park

Admission: Free (some programmes require registration)

Best For: Families / Culture Seekers / Free Activities / Nature Lovers

Concierge Recommendation: This closes on the 13th, so it's a genuine last-call this week – the free weekend shuttle bus makes it easy to combine both parks in one visit without arranging separate transport.

Homegrown Festival

Now in its third edition, Homegrown Festival transforms Paya Lebar Quarter Plaza into a free outdoor music festival spotlighting Singapore's own artists. This year's lineup is headlined by contemporary R&B trio brb. and breakout indie-pop artist Regina Song, alongside a festival village of homegrown brands and the Homegrown Rising youth band competition.

Event Date: 11–13 September 2026

Location: Paya Lebar Quarter Plaza

Admission: Free

Best For: Young Adults / Music Fans / Free Activities

Concierge Recommendation: A good, free evening option for guests who want a genuine taste of Singapore's local music scene rather than an international act.

Mid-Autumn Light-Up at Gardens by the Bay

Gardens by the Bay's giant lantern displays return for Mid-Autumn Festival, illuminating the gardens with photogenic, large-scale setups – a family favourite that kicks off the wider Mid-Autumn season across the city.

Event Date: From 11 September 2026 (weekend)

Location: Gardens by the Bay

Best For: Families / Photography / Free Activities

Concierge Recommendation: An easy add-on for any guest already visiting Gardens by the Bay this week – best enjoyed after sunset.

Kreta Ayer Mid-Autumn Festival

Chinatown's Kreta Ayer neighbourhood marks Mid-Autumn Festival with community lantern displays, a procession, lantern riddles and free family activities – a more traditional, neighbourhood-level alternative to the larger citywide light-ups.

Event Date: 11 September – 4 October 2026

Location: Kreta Ayer, Chinatown

Admission: Free

Best For: Families / Culture Seekers / Free Activities

Concierge Recommendation: A good pick for guests wanting a more authentic, community-level Mid-Autumn experience rather than a large-scale commercial display.

#RevUpSG – Spanish Grand Prix Screening

Part of the build-up to the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026, this free community watch party brings the Spanish Grand Prix to a big screen in the heartlands, with a festival atmosphere, interactive games and F1 merchandise giveaways.

Event Date: 12–13 September 2026

Time: 12:30pm–11:00pm both days (qualifying 10:00pm Sat, race 9:00pm Sun)

Location: HDB Hub, Toa Payoh (6 min walk from Toa Payoh MRT)

Admission: Free

Best For: Motorsport Fans / Free Activities / Families

Concierge Recommendation: A fun, free option for F1 fans staying nearby – good to know as the city builds toward the Singapore Grand Prix itself in October.

Restaurants & Bars

Tian Tian Chicken Rice – New Jewel Changi Outlet

Tian Tian hardly needs an introduction to anyone who follows Singapore's hawker scene. Founded in 1986 by Madam Foo Kui Lian at Maxwell Food Centre, it's been praised by the late Anthony Bourdain, beaten Gordon Ramsay in a televised Hawker Heroes cook-off, and held a Michelin Bib Gourmand continuously since 2016. Its new outlet brings that same chicken rice to a nearly 100-seat space in the basement of Jewel Changi Airport, right next to Food Republic – making it one of the few genuinely famous hawker names accessible without leaving the airport.

Location: Jewel Changi Airport, Basement, next to Food Republic

Signature: Chicken Rice Set ($11++, steamed or roasted); Madam Foo's Steamed Chicken Curry ($13.80++, a rarer find outside the original Maxwell stall)

Best For: Solo Diners / Layover Guests / Hawker Food Fans / Departing Guests

Concierge Recommendation: Genuinely useful for guests on a layover or heading to the airport early – this is one of the only ways to try a properly famous hawker stall without a special trip into town. Expect queues; the chicken rice alone is worth the wait.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Palm Beach Seafood

Located at One Fullerton, right where the Singapore River meets Marina Bay and within sight of the Merlion, Palm Beach Seafood has been serving Singapore-style seafood for decades. Guests can choose air-conditioned indoor seating or the alfresco terrace, where the breeze and the bay view do a lot of the work. The restaurant's Chilli Crab has become one of its signature dishes over the years, alongside Black Pepper Crab and its own Coco-Lobo creation.

Current Promotion: None advertised – check for seasonal crab promotions.

Reservation Policy: Recommended, especially for alfresco seating at sunset; no credit card required to book.

Hours: Daily, 12:00pm–2:30pm & 5:30pm–10:30pm

Contact: +65 6336 8118

Address: 1 Fullerton Road, #01-09, One Fullerton, Singapore 049213

Concierge Recommendation: A reliable pick for guests wanting the classic Singapore chilli crab experience with a proper view – request the alfresco terrace specifically if guests want the Marina Bay backdrop.

Gunther's Modern French Cuisine

Tucked into Purvis Street in the Civic District, Gunther's has built a loyal following around Chef-Owner Gunther Hubrechsen's reinterpretation of French classics. Hubrechsen trained under Chef Alain Passard in 1998, and that ingredient-forward, vegetable-conscious philosophy still shows in how the menu is built – refined without feeling stiff, in a cozy dining room that leans more intimate than grand.

Current Promotion: Seasonal set lunch, changes monthly – confirm current offering directly.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required; WhatsApp or call directly. Closed Sundays.

Hours: Daily except Sunday, lunch and dinner (confirm exact hours when booking)

Contact: +65 9010 3075 (also WhatsApp)

Address: 36 Purvis Street, #01-03, Singapore 188613

Signature: Cold angel hair pasta with caviar; roasted suckling pig

Concierge Recommendation: A dependable, slightly lower-key alternative to the bigger-name French restaurants in town – good for guests wanting quality without the formality. Remind them it's closed Sundays.

Hotel & Hospitality News

SKAI – Toy Story Afternoon Tea

SKAI, the contemporary grill on the 70th floor of Swissotel The Stamford, has introduced a Toy Story-themed afternoon tea – character-inspired treats served against the same panoramic city views the restaurant is known for. A playful, family-friendly addition to a venue more typically associated with skyline dining and sharing plates.

Event Date: 1 September – 30 November 2026

Time: Daily, 12:15pm–5:30pm

Location: Level 70, Swissotel The Stamford, 2 Stamford Road, Singapore 178882

Contact: +65 6837 3322

Note: Not halal-certified

Best For: Families / Toy Story Fans / Skyline Views

Concierge Recommendation: A fun option for families wanting a skyline experience that isn't a full dinner commitment – worth flagging the halal status upfront if relevant to the guest.

Transport & Operational Updates

Singapore Gallery Month & SLA25 Trail – Final Day

Both Singapore Gallery Month and the SLA25 Rediscovery Trail close on 13 September. This is the last chance to send guests to either before they wrap up for the year.

Overnight Expressway & Tunnel Works

Several routine overnight closures continue this week, all outside normal guest travel hours: TPE/PIE slip roads near Tampines Ave 7 and Loyang Ave close 10:00pm–5:30am on various nights through 12 September for bridge works; KPE Tunnel slip roads close 12:00am–5:00am on 7, 9, 10 and 12 September for maintenance; CTE Tunnel closes 12:00am–5:00am on 8 September for the same reason. Lentor Avenue also has nightly closures (1:30am–5:30am) continuing through the month for North-South Corridor construction. None of these affect typical guest activity, but worth knowing for anyone with a very early transfer.

Bras Basah.Bugis, Riverside & National Stadium Crowds

Expect heavier foot traffic around the river precincts from 11 September (Singapore River Festival) and around the National Stadium on 12–13 September (AL!VE Artisans Market).

Hungry Ghost Festival Continues

The Hungry Ghost Festival continues through 10 September – nearly over by the end of this edition's window. See Edition 007 for full background if needed.

Looking Ahead

Singapore Tennis Open – WTA 500

The newly upgraded Singapore Tennis Open, now a WTA 500 tournament, runs 21–27 September at OCBC Arena – among the top-tier events on the WTA calendar, with single-session tickets from $8. Worth flagging early to any guests interested in tennis.

Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix Season Build-Up

With the Singapore Grand Prix itself running 9–11 October, expect community fan events and city-wide buzz to build steadily over the coming weeks.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Singapore Gallery Month and SLA25 Rediscovery Trail both close 13 September – this is a final call, not a routine mention.

  • Tian Tian's new Jewel Changi outlet is a great last-minute recommendation for departing guests – mention it specifically to anyone heading to the airport with time to spare.

  • Gunther's is closed on Sundays – confirm before recommending for a Sunday dinner.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day — Riverside Evening

Evening: Pick one zone of the Singapore River Festival – Boat Quay for entertainment, Clarke Quay for the Expression Zone, or Robertson Quay for a quieter Lifestyle & Wellness experience.

Tip: Dinner at Palm Beach Seafood (One Fullerton) sits right at the edge of the festival zones – an easy way to combine both.

Full Day — Heritage Last Call

Morning: SLA25 Rediscovery Trail stop at Alkaff Mansion or 195 Pearl's Hill Terrace – last chance before it closes on the 13th.

Afternoon: Singapore Gallery Month galleries at Gillman Barracks or Tanjong Pagar Distripark, also closing the 13th.

Evening: Dinner at Gunther's in the Civic District.

Tip: Both closing attractions are free and don't require booking – easy to fit into a single day without advance planning.

2 Days — River & Market Weekend

Day 1

Afternoon: AL!VE Artisans Market at National Stadium. Evening: Singapore River Festival at Clarke Quay.

Day 2

Morning: SKAI's Toy Story Afternoon Tea (families) or a Botanic Gardens visit with lunch at Tembusu. Evening: Dinner at Palm Beach Seafood or Gunther's.

Tip: SKAI's afternoon tea runs from 12:15pm – book ahead if travelling with children, as it's proven popular since launch.

Quick Reference

Best Free Riverside Event: Singapore River Festival 2026

Best Low-Key Market: AL!VE Artisans Market

Best Airport Dining: Tian Tian Chicken Rice (Jewel Changi)

Best Family Skyline Experience: SKAI's Toy Story Afternoon Tea

Best Classic Seafood: Palm Beach Seafood

Best Civic District French Dining: Gunther's Modern French Cuisine

Best Last-Chance Pick: Singapore Gallery Month & SLA25 Rediscovery Trail (close 13 Sep)
